quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 1 (KA)/TD03786_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I MAN NGAG GI BSTAN BCOS MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN ZHES BYA BA'I TSIG LE'UR BYAS PA (Abhisamayālaṃkāra Nāma Prajñā Pāramita Upadeśa Śāstra Kārikā)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: The root verse: the six abhijñās are the seventh of the ten instructions (གདམས་ངག) under sarvākārajñatā — the lemma the whole section, and this paragraph, hangs from.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 7 (JA)/TD03793_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I MAN NGAG GI BSTAN BCOS MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN ZHES BYA BA'I 'GREL PA (Abhisamayālaṃkāra Nāma Prajñā Pāramita Upadeśa Śāstra Vṛtti)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: Haribhadra's one-sentence gloss, from which the paragraph lifts all six of its དེའི་དོན་འཆད་པ་ལ quotations — and whose closing clause (གཟོད་མ་ནས་ཞི་བ) is what the next paragraph, p417, takes up.

The divine-eye sūtra passage in the eight-chapter recension of the Pañcaviṃśati, whose wording — ལས་ཇི་ལྟ་བ་བཞིན་…ཉེ་བར་འགྲོ་བ — the yig cha's quotation follows, where the Kangyur text reads differently.
The āsravakṣaya sūtra passage in the eight-chapter recension — མི་སྐྱེ་བ་མངོན་དུ་བྱེད་པ, མི་ལྟུང་, སྨོན་པར་མི་བྱེད — the wording the yig cha quotes.

quotes.file: Kangyur/3. NYI KHRI (Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 1 (KA)/KL00009E1INC_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STONG PHRAG NYI SHU LNGA PA 1_The Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines, Part 1 (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā 1)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: The same passage as the Kangyur Pañcaviṃśati gives it: ཟག་པ་ཟད་པ་མངོན་དུ་བྱ་བ and ས་ཐོབ་པར་མི་བྱེད, not the yig cha's wording — evidence that the yig cha cites the eight-chapter recension.

quotes.file: Kangyur/3. NYI KHRI (Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 1 (KA)/KL00009E1INC_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STONG PHRAG NYI SHU LNGA PA 1_The Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines, Part 1 (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā 1)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: The Kangyur form of the summarising sentence, which lacks the paragraph's ཡོངས་སུ་དག་པར་བྱེད་དོ.
The eight-chapter recension's summarising sentence, matching the paragraph's closing quotation word for word.
What the paragraph's ཞེས་སོགས hides: each abhijñā passage in the sūtra closes by saying the bodhisattva does not apprehend the power or grow conceited over it.
Tsongkhapa's instruction to read Haribhadra's two lists of six as names and meanings respectively — the division the yig cha adopts for p415 and p416.
Tsongkhapa on how the divine eye of the five eyes differs from the divine-eye abhijñā: Haribhadra follows Vimuktisena — past karma versus present meditation.
Ārya Vimuktisena's own statement of the difference, the source of Haribhadra's qualifier མངོན་པར་འདུ་བྱེད་པ་ལས་བྱུང་བ on the divine eye.
Tsongkhapa: the eye and ear abhijñās rely on faculties, the other four on mind — the formulation behind the later dispute over whether these two are sense consciousnesses.
Tsongkhapa keeps Haribhadra's two obscurations in the gloss on āsravakṣaya, adding 'has abandoned or is abandoning'.
Gyaltsab Je: the divine eye itself is clear form of the meditative level; the abhijñā is a mental consciousness that has it as dominant condition.
Gyaltsab Je's account of āsravakṣaya in terms of both obscurations — the wording Chökyi Gyaltsen's opponent turns into a definition.
Panchen Sonam Drakpa (Loseling) holding that the རྣམ་བཤད's account of the divine eye as clear form, with a sense-consciousness abhijñā, must be read as provisional.

quotes.text: ཉན་ཐོས་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པའི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་ཟག་ཟད་ཀྱི་མངོན་ཤེས་ཆོས་ཅན། མཚན་ཉིད་དྲུག་པ་དེར་ཐལ། མཚོན་བྱ་དེའི་ཕྱིར། རྟགས་གྲུབ་སྟེ། ཆོས་ཅན་དེའི་ཕྱིར། འདོད་ན། སྒྲིབ་གཉིས་སྤངས་པའི་བྲལ་བ་མངོན་སུམ་དུ་རྟོགས་པར་ཐལ། འདོད་པའི་ཕྱིར། འདོད་མི་ནུས་ཏེ། སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་རྒྱུད་ཀྱི་ཤེས་པ་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར།
quotes.why: Chökyi Gyaltsen refuting a definition of āsravakṣaya built on 'both obscurations': a śrāvaka arhat has the abhijñā but has not abandoned the jñeyāvaraṇa.
Chökyi Gyaltsen denying that the divine-eye and divine-ear abhijñās are sense consciousnesses.
Chökyi Gyaltsen's own definitions of the fifth and sixth abhijñās: the divine eye as dominant condition, and the kleśāvaraṇa alone for āsravakṣaya.
Chökyi Gyaltsen's boundary for the Mahāyāna āsravakṣaya abhijñā: a concordant form from the eighth ground, the actual one only at buddhahood.
Chökyi Gyaltsen's syllogism on the same sūtra: it instructs in the six abhijñās as existing conventionally and not ultimately.

quotes.file: Tengyur/07 MNGON PA_Higher Knowledge School (Abhidharma)/VOL 2 (KU)/TD04089_CHOS MNGON PA'I MDZOD KYI TSIG LE'UR BYAS PA (Abhidarmakoṣa Kārikā)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: Vasubandhu's Abhidharmakośa on the ethical status of the eye and ear abhijñās, cited by Tsongkhapa here and argued over in Chökyi Gyaltsen's mtha' dpyod.

quotes.file: Kangyur/3. NYI KHRI (Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 1 (KA)/KL00009E1INC_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STONG PHRAG NYI SHU LNGA PA 1_The Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines, Part 1 (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā 1)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: The Kangyur sūtra ties the bodhisattva's āsravakṣaya to the vajra-like samādhi and to abandoning afflictions together with their imprints — the end of the path, which is where Chökyi Gyaltsen places the actual Mahāyāna form.
Jamyang Zhepa (Gomang) classing every abhijñā as mental direct perception — the Drepung Gomang side of the sense-or-mental question.
